challenge.method: Tested whether the 1.0 and 1.1 URLs could be exchanged without changing the evidence. Compared the titles, opening notices and section 1 definitions, checked which edition the 2017 decision actually releases, and matched the editorial row by entity ID, scope and documentary revision.
challenge.results: Exchanging the URLs fails both the notice and body-text checks. The 1.0 definition of distribution describes making copies available. The corresponding 1.1 definition adds access to essential functionalities. The 2017 decision releases 1.2 and identifies 1.0 in its recitals. The 1.0 editorial row matches the claimed entity and preserves the qualification condition.

limitations: The web observation covers the visible English representation. Original PDF byte identity, adoption dates, equivalence across languages, redistribution, installation and grants for a particular work are outside this finding.
The statement carries the qualification condition. The empty conditions array and the value active, read alone, do not establish that admission and review gates have passed.
reasoning: The English document at the CIRCABC URL identifies itself as EUPL v.1.0 in both its title and its opening notice. The Index decision assigns the corresponding prospective entity the display name European Union Public Licence v. 1.0, kind license and state active upon qualification.
